consensus.title: Position 1 on the big roofing searches is a map-pack position, not a blue link
consensus.body: The ten largest queries ("roofing companies," "roofers," "roofing contractors near me") total 11,717 impressions and 1 click at positions 1 to 3. All four research engines agree this is not a normal first-place ranking. Google gives every link inside a result block, such as the local map pack or an AI Overview, the position of the block itself, and a call or directions tap from the map never counts as a website click. September: pull the Search Appearance breakdown for these queries, confirm which homepage URL is entered in the Business Profile, and report Business Profile calls next to the SEO numbers.

consensus.title: August's click gain came entirely from the homepage
consensus.body: Clicks rose from 186 to 222, a gain of 36. The homepage alone rose from 102 to 138, also 36. Every other page combined produced 84 clicks in July and 84 in August. So the headline growth is a homepage and brand story, not broad search growth, and part of it may be job seekers searching the company name during the office-manager campaign. Read the month as steady, not surging. Filter job-related queries out of Search Console before crediting the growth, and set the September target as non-homepage clicks above 84.

consensus.title: Trust the real numbers; the 78% traffic-value drop is a model, not a loss
consensus.body: The estimate formula is verified from the vendor documentation: search volume times a fixed click rate for each position, then times the ad cost per click. Estimated traffic fell 58% and estimated value fell 78%, which only means the keywords that slipped were expensive ones. Meanwhile actual clicks rose 19.4%, organic sessions rose 19.9% with 60.4% engagement, and 24 qualified leads came in. Report order: qualified leads, organic sessions, Search Console clicks, then rankings. Label the estimate "modeled traffic estimate, not observed traffic or revenue" and keep it off the headline.

consensus.title: Cost searches now route through the financing page
consensus.body: /budget-roof-cost lost 80% of its impressions (3,764 to 745) after the dollar figures came out. All four research engines call price removal the main cause, with the restructure secondary. Since the rule stands, serve the intent differently: "roofing payment plans" already shows 1,074 impressions at position 12 and belongs to /roof-financing-options, which grew to 4,997 impressions. September: sharpen the top of the financing page (plans, application steps, when payments start, what qualifies), and have the quote-factors page explain what changes an estimate and point to financing and to a written estimate request. No numbers anywhere.

consensus.title: Refresh five pages that already rank instead of writing five new blogs
consensus.body: Fifteen pages sit in the top 20 with impressions and zero clicks. Two engines independently pick the same targets: the hail damage guide (292 impressions, position 19), the choosing-a-contractor article (265, 16.6), winter siding (151, 8.8), can-it-wait-until-spring (119, 10.2), and the HOA damage post (111, 10.3). For each: a title that states the answer, the direct answer in the first 80 words, two to four links into the repair, replacement, and siding service pages, one service CTA. Keep the URLs. Leave black streaks (clicks doubled at flat rank) and ice dams alone.

consensus.title: The one structural job: an internal-link sprint tied to a 12-query map
consensus.body: Freeze 12 target queries and the single page each should win: roof replacement, roof repair, financing, siding, James Hardie, commercial, quote factors, contractor choice, homepage. Then add about 15 in-body links from blog posts and high-traffic pages into those service pages with varied, natural anchors. Roof replacement drove 15 of 24 unique leads yet its page sits at position 17.4 with one click; repairs sit at 17.4 with one click. Links are the cheapest authority the site has not used. Generic "roofers" and "near me" terms belong in the Business Profile column, not the organic target list.

consensus.title: Separate the job-post traffic in GA4, do not delete it
consensus.body: 999 paid-social sessions at 5.9 seconds pushed /careers to the top page and inflated every sitewide total. All four research engines say the same thing: no permanent property filter. Instead: a custom channel group named Recruiting, a saved comparison that excludes sessions landing on /careers, an annotation with the campaign start and end dates, and UTM tags on future job posts. Then rerun August organic (356 sessions) with careers excluded before calling it customer growth. Show two views every month: total site and customer acquisition.

consensus.title: Bing is the ChatGPT lever, and it is cheap
consensus.body: ChatGPT visibility is 16% against Gemini 39% and Perplexity 48%, yet one of nine AI-referred visits in August became a qualified lead. OpenAI's own help center confirms ChatGPT passes searches to Bing and only includes sites its search crawler can reach. Verify the site in Bing Webmaster Tools, submit the sitemap, and inspect the homepage, replacement, repair, financing and siding pages. One afternoon of work. The late-August off-site rebuild cannot show up until September or October data, so judge it then, not now.

disagreements.title: Gutter page after cooling: links in, or a title change?
disagreements.body: Perplexity and ARI want the title moved toward repair and replacement. OpenAI and Gemini say do not touch the page, add links to it. A live check settles it: the title already reads "Gutter Repair & Installation in the Lehigh Valley," so the retitle has nothing to fix. Resolution: once cooling ends late September, add five in-body links from the gutter-signs blog, the FAQ page, the ice-dam post and the siding page, and judge success on a fixed set of gutter repair and replacement queries (now at 34.2 and 44.6), not the page average of 23.7. Until then, only export the query list.

disagreements.title: Which number should headline the monthly report
disagreements.body: OpenAI wants customer-intent Search Console clicks with the homepage caveat. ARI wants qualified organic leads. Gemini wants GA4 organic sessions plus form submissions. Resolution: leads first (24 qualified), GA4 organic sessions second (356, restated with careers traffic excluded), Search Console clicks third with the "non-homepage flat at 84" note, then rankings. The modeled traffic value never headlines and always carries its label. This order matches how the business actually feels a good month: forms and calls, then engaged visitors, then clicks.

disagreements.title: Rewrite the zero-click titles now, or skip them
disagreements.body: Gemini wants five title rewrites this month: Wind Gap, Wyomissing, New Tripoli, /contact and /james-hardie. OpenAI says no blanket rewrites: pages at positions 20 to 36 will not earn clicks from a new title, /roof-cost is a redirect, not a page, /contact at position 6.1 is mostly brand traffic, and /our-blog shows "No blog posts found" in its raw HTML, so its rendering needs fixing before its title. Resolution: Wind Gap (1,052 impressions, position 14.1) gets one controlled title and description change. The five refreshed blog posts carry their own new titles. Nothing else.

disagreements.title: Why Perplexity fell nine points
disagreements.body: Gemini blames incomplete off-site profiles. OpenAI and ARI point out nothing changed off-site until August 27, and a constant cannot explain a change. Cited pages fell from 39 to 34 with no site changes, which fits Perplexity rotating its sources between runs. Resolution: treat the 57 to 48 drop as noise until it repeats. Run the same 204 prompts in September and compare platform by platform. The overall score moved one point (35 to 34), so nothing about August suggests a real visibility loss.

anomalies.title: 46 keywords at #1 versus one true organic #1
anomalies.body: The tracking tool reports 46 tracked keywords at position 1, up from 41, while its own organic distribution shows exactly one keyword at position 1. Same split as July: the 46 count feature placements (41 AI Overview references, local pack wins, best-rank consolidation), the distribution counts blue links only. Both are correct, they measure different things. Report them as "AI and feature placements" and "organic rankings" on separate lines and never compare them directly.

anomalies.title: The homepage shows up twice in Search Console
anomalies.body: Both alternate homepage URLs redirect in one hop to the https version (verified), yet Search Console still splits the homepage into one row at position 1.9 (17,676 impressions, 92 clicks) and another at 19.2 (16,717 impressions, 46 clicks). The likely reason: one exact URL string is stored in the Business Profile website field and inherits the map-pack position, while the other is the real organic result. Set the Business Profile website to the https address with a tracking tag and watch whether the split closes.

anomalies.title: The live site still contradicts the standing rules
anomalies.body: The brief says all prices came out in July, and a live check confirms the homepage, financing page, and quote-factors page show no dollar figures (one research engine claimed otherwise and was wrong). But the homepage still leads its repair copy with urgent-response wording and features a roofing material the company does not want emphasized. And the financing page markets plans whose own descriptions read "Same as Cash" and "Deferred Interest" under a "True 0% Interest" headline. Confirm the wording with the lender and clean up the copy before promoting the page.

anomalies.title: A Google spam update landed in the last two weeks of August
anomalies.body: Google's status dashboard confirms an August 2026 spam update running August 18 to 21. It was not in the brief and none of the four research engines mentioned it. Valley Peak shows no penalty signs: clicks rose, average position improved, and no new spam policies were announced. But any late-August dip in a specific page should be checked against that date before it gets blamed on July's content changes. Split August in Search Console at August 18 and compare the two halves.
